originalTitle: ICE to spend up to $20m on gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks
summary: According to manufacturer, shock ‘is usually effective in bringing individuals into compliance in less than three seconds’
content: ICE plans to spend up to $20m (£15m) to purchase thousands of gloves that can deliver painful electric shocks for officers and agents by March, according to a notice published Monday by the Department of Homeland Security. The devices, called Glove (Generated Low Output Voltage Emitter), are manufactured by Compliant Technologies LLC of Lexington, Kentucky. According to the manufacturer, “the discomfort associated with the stimulation is usually effective in bringing individuals into compliance in less than three seconds and leaves no burns, marks or scars”. The company has advertised the device as a “humane, low-optics, de-escalation solution for many situations facing our men and women in uniform”. The gloves have previously been used in settings such as jails in the US. Compliant Technologies says the devices function as a normal pair of patrol gloves until officers press a switch to activate their electrical mode. The gloves must be applied directly to someone’s skin to deliver a pain stimulus that typically helps an officer gain compliance within seconds, according to the company. “It’s immediate and sharp, and it will distract you. I call it like a bee sting,” said John Peters, president of the Institute for the Prevention of In-Custody Deaths, who is studying how the device has been used. “If the officer is getting any type of resistance from the person, this is certainly an effective tool.” Civil rights advocates expressed alarm at the plan, saying ICE officers already face criticism for their use of force with little oversight or accountability while enforcing Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown. Jenn Rolnick Borchetta, deputy project director on policing at the American Civil Liberties Union, told the Associated Press that she questioned the use of the devices for civil immigration enforcement. “ICE spent the last year showing this country they are too quick to use force. Now they will be able to deploy electric shocks with the slight push of a button that maybe nobody else can see them do,” she said. “Introducing gloves that can so easily be used to deliver terrible pain in encounters is a recipe for harm to the public.” Peters said he believed ICE’s planned purchase would likely be the largest from the company to date. He said he could envision ICE officers using the gloves to help remove uncooperative subjects from cars and houses and in and out of detention facilities. The manufacturer warns the device should not be used as punishment, against people merely exhibiting “verbal defiance or belligerence” or on high-risk populations such as children, pregnant women or elderly or disabled people. Jeff Niklaus, the founder and CEO of Compliant Technologies, wrote in an email: “Unfortunately, we are unable to speak on this subject.”
chineseTitle: ICE 将斥资 2000 万美元购买可带来痛苦电击的手套
chineseSummary: 据制造商称，电击“通常可以在不到三秒的时间内有效地使个人服从”
chineseContent: 根据国土安全部周一发布的通知，ICE 计划在 3 月份之前斥资 2000 万美元（1500 万英镑）购买数千副手套，这些手套可以为官员和特工带来痛苦的电击。这些设备称为 Glove（生成低输出电压发射器），由肯塔基州列克星敦的 Compliant Technologies LLC 制造。根据制造商的说法，“与刺激相关的不适通常可以有效地在不到三秒的时间内使个人服从，并且不会留下烧伤、痕迹或疤痕”。该公司将该设备宣传为“一种人性化、低光学、降级解决方案，适用于我们穿制服的男女所面临的许多情况”。这种手套此前曾在美国监狱等环境中使用过。 Compliant Technologies 表示，这些设备的功能就像一副普通的巡逻手套，直到警察按下开关激活其电动模式。该公司表示，手套必须直接戴在某人的皮肤上，以产生疼痛刺激，通常可以帮助警官在几秒钟内获得服从。 “它是直接的、尖锐的，而且会分散你的注意力。我称其为蜜蜂蜇伤，”正在研究该装置如何使用的防止羁押期间死亡研究所所长约翰·彼得斯 (John Peters) 说。 “如果警官受到此人任何类型的抵抗，这无疑是一个有效的工具。”民权倡导者对该计划表示震惊，称ICE官员在执行唐纳德·特朗普的移民镇压行动时，已经因在缺乏监督或问责的情况下使用武力而受到批评。美国公民自由联盟警务项目副主任 Jenn Rolnick Borchetta 告诉美联社，她对该设备的使用提出质疑
whyItMatters: 这条信息属于全球新闻信号，适合用于观察外部环境、政策变化、地缘风险和市场情绪。
